author: Suzette Lowe FOR JACKSON NEWSPAPERS
title: Commission approves $1.5M radio upgrade, weighs funding for library and local events | Jackson Star and Herald - Ripley and Ravenswood | wvnews.com
text:
RIPLEY, W.Va. — The Jackson County Commission reviewed an array of funding requests ranging from infrastructure repairs to community wellness initiatives during its May 6 meeting, headlined by the approval of a $1.5 million radio system upgrade for emergency responders.
Jackson County Library Board Director Carla Long and board member Katrena Ramsey presented an urgent request regarding the Ripley branch.
"Our roof is leaking profusely," Long said. "We're doing much better with our finances, but the bid we chose was $54,250, an amount that's difficult to come up with all at once. If you have any extra funds, that would be amazing."
Long noted that Above Roofing was the winning bidder. The company, which she said comes highly recommended, will install an inside roof access hatch at no cost.
Commission President Steve Westfall said the matter would be taken under advisement.
Jennifer Scritchfield, an organizer for the annual Women’s Wellness Retreat, requested continued support for the event's fifth year, scheduled for Sept. 12 at the Parchment Valley Conference Center.
"This is a unique opportunity for women to come for mental, physical, emotional, and financial guidance," Scritchfield said. "We have branched out to work with women in recovery as well."
The commission, which allocated $1,000 for the retreat last year, is expected to make a decision at a future meeting.
The Jackson County Development Authority (JCDA) and Downtown Ravenswood Partners also sought permission and signatures for specialized projects.
JCDA Director Veronica Lewis said the organization is applying for a West Virginia Division of Economic Development grant to fund expansion and a turning lane into the TIMET facility.
"This resolution is something I need to be able to move forward," Lewis said. "The cost cannot exceed the grant, so there will be no expense for the county. One of the key elements of development will be completing these industrial access roads."
Molly Washburn and Jennifer Casey of Downtown Ravenswood Partners presented a mural project proposed for the former Hupp’s Ice Cream building, a prominent site for those entering the city.
"The outside of the building does not reflect the investment made to the inside by my husband and me," Casey said. "The mural will pay homage to businesses that were very prosperous in Ravenswood's history."
A $5,000 grant from the West Virginia Department of Tourism is slated to fund the project.
"We don't know of any other organization in the county asking for this grant, so we would appreciate the commission allowing us to apply," Washburn said.
Local artist Neil LoPrinzi will lead the project, assisted by Philip Moulton and an additional unnamed artist.
In further action, commissioners approved an America 250 grant request with a completion deadline of May 31, 2026.
The session’s largest approved expenditure, totaling $1,549,198.30, allows Jackson County 911 to upgrade its radio system. The project aims to dramatically improve coverage, clarity, and reliability for emergency responders countywide.
911 Director Montana Boggess, who has spearheaded the effort for several years, said after the meeting that the upgrade is the county's largest emergency communication project to date.
"We are proud to partner with Zetron, a highly respected international company with a proven track record in public safety," Boggess said. "We are equally thankful that the county commission supported and recognized the importance of this project."
Officials estimate the new system will take 18 months to fully integrate.
In other business, Commissioners Dick Waybright, Mitch Morrison, and Westfall:
- Heard a $5,000 request from Peter Coffey, director of Parchment Valley Conference Center, for the Brothers Keeper program.
- Approved Drawdown 29 for $26,287.75 for the Ravenswood Sewer Phase 2A, utilizing American Relief Plan Act (ARPA) funds.
- Noted a vacancy in the county IT department.
- Approved a $63,648 contract with W. Q. Watters Company for the clock tower painting project.
- Allocated $500 for the Ohio River Festival for fiscal year 2026-27 and $5,000 for Vets 4 Vets.
- Approved a $1,550 monthly contract with Maddox Hollow Excavating and Agriculture Services LLC for mowing at the Walter Smittle Training Center.
- Approved State Budget Revision No. 5 to the general fund.
- Acknowledged the resignations of IT Specialist Joel Fisher and Deputy Anthony Crow, effective April 24, 2026.
- Approved hiring Brayden Coe as a sheriff's deputy at $21.67 per hour, effective May 16, 2026.
- Approved a $2,500 contract with Dean-Ray Contracting for new drop ceilings in the circuit court judge's offices.
- Approved a $15,000 West Virginia Department of Agriculture Spay and Neuter Grant with a $3,750 match.
- Approved a $9,901.25 Division of Multimodal Transportation Facilities grant for airport improvements.
- Approved a $10,000 Records Management and Preservation Grant for the county clerk’s office.
- Allocated $10,700 to the Southern Jackson Public Service District for sewer expansion using remaining ARPA interest.
The commission entered executive session at 10:16 a.m. to discuss real estate negotiations regarding the Jackson County Airport and personnel matters for the Sheriff’s Office.
Attending the session were the three commissioners, County Attorney Eric Holmes, JCDA Director Lewis, County Administrator Julia Gump, and Airport Director Sam Dennis. The second session included the commissioners, the attorney, the county administrator, Sheriff Ross Mellinger, Lieutenant Gary Baldwin, and Captain Todd Roberts.
No action was taken upon reconvening.
The next meeting is scheduled for Wednesday, May 20, 2026, at 9:30 a.m.
